Indian Constitution at Work
Chapter Two
RIGHTS IN THE INDIAN
CONSTITUTION
INTRODUCTION
A constitution is not only about the composition of the various organs of
government and the relations among them. As we studied in the last chapter,
the constitution is a document that sets limits on the powers of the government
and ensures a democratic system in which all persons enjoy certain rights. In this

correctItems.text: A team of social scientists studied their poor condition and petitioned the Supreme Court.
They argued that employing a person to work for less than the minimum prescribed wage amounts to begar or forced labour, which is a violation of the Fundamental Right against exploitation.
The court accepted this plea and directed the government to ensure that thousands of workers get the prescribed wages for their work.
A resident of Chuburi village of Morigaon district of Assam, Machal was charged of causing grievous injuries.

They argued that employing a person to work for less than the minimum prescribed wage amounts to begar or forced labour, which is a violation of the Fundamental Right against exploitation.

A resident of Chuburi village of Morigaon district of Assam, Machal was charged of causing grievous injuries.
